extracted.intended_audience: members of Congress, patent practitioners, inventors, PTO staff, and patent policy stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and policy provisions used to evaluate or craft provisions of the America Invents Act (H.R. 1249) — focusing on patentability rules, PTO funding and operations, procedural protections (grace period, prior art, post-grant review), and specific substantive exclusions. Relevant for assessing how legislative changes affect patent quality, litigation, and innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent quality and examination rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure newly-issued patents are "strong, high-quality patents that have gone through rigorous review."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poor-quality patents issued due to examiner backlog do significant damage (e.g., used by nonpracticing entities to demand rents). Improving patent quality requires giving examiners sufficient time and resources to review applications. Legislative provisions should enable the PTO to reduce issuance of 'dubious' patents that 'should have been denied.'

rubrics_metrics.name: PTO funding — end fee diversion / reserve fund
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide mechanisms so the Patent Office can retain and access the fees it collects (end fee diversion); establish an exclusive PTO reserve fund to collect excess PTO fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All excess fees collected by the PTO "will be deposited into the PTO reserve fund and amounts in the fund 'shall be made available until expended only for obligation and expenditure by the Office.'" The reserve fund is intended to 'wall-off PTO funds from diversion' while preserving congressional oversight via appropriations. Access should include availability during continuing resolutions and reasonable treatment of reprogramming requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTO access to fees at all times (including continuing resolutions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide USPTO access to all fees collected at all points during the fiscal year, including in case of a continuing resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing access 'at all points during that year' means appropriations language should appropriate any fees collected in excess of the requested level and provide a clear mechanism for PTO to request access to those funds; this supports the agency's ability to reduce backlog and improve patent quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce patent application backlog
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislation should enable the USPTO to reduce the backlog of patent applications (noted as exceeding 700,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Backlog reduction requires sufficient PTO funding and operational reform so examiners can spend adequate time per application. Without access to fee collections, PTO cannot properly plan or implement changes needed to reduce pendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-to-file implementation contingent on grace period/prior art fix
rubrics_metrics.description: The move to a first-to-file system 'would not go into effect until the grace period ... actually is fixed and harmonized' and until the fatal defects in defining prior art (disclosures) are remedied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proponents argue harmonization with other countries is desirable, but critics urge that first-to-file must preserve the critical U.S. 'grace period' and that prior art definitions (what counts as a disclosure) must be clarified to avoid disadvantaging inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify prior art definition / fix disclosures defect
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments should remedy the 'fatal defect of defining the prior art is disclosures' so prior art is properly defined under the new scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if manager's amendments are supported, they may not fully remedy prior art definition issues. Lawmakers recommended stepping back to examine prior-user rights and the grace period and to preserve the U.S. 'gold standard' grace period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expansion/clarification of prior-user rights (section 273)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislative text expands and clarifies prior-user rights under section 273 of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly strengthening prior-user rights is a listed provision in the manager's amendment, intended to protect parties who commercially used an invention prior to another's filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business-method transitional post-grant review program
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a transitional program within the PTO to evaluate business-method patents using 'the best prior art available.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is intended to weed out 'bad' business-method patents while allowing 'good ones' to become legally stronger. It creates a mechanism for targeted post-issuance review focused on business-method patents that were issued over the past decade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant review (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include post-grant review procedures as part of patent reform (though contested by some as potentially harmful).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supporters view post-grant review as a tool to remove poor patents; critics argue it 'does more harm than good' and express concern about retroactively undoing court decisions or creating uncertainty. Design of scope and timing matter for balancing benefits and risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best mode disclosure — retain as specification requirement but not litigation basis
rubrics_metrics.description: "Best mode" remains a specifications requirement for obtaining a patent, but once the examiner is satisfied, best mode cannot be used as a defense in infringement litigation or as a basis for post-grant review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change preserves the disclosure obligation but removes best mode as a litigation weapon. The intent is to reduce lawsuit abuse while maintaining disclosure to examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit patenting of "human organism" (Weldon amendment codification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include language that forbids the patenting of inventions 'directed to or encompassing a human organism.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provision codifies an existing PTO policy/rider (the Weldon amendment since FY2004) and reflects the position that no human being is 'an invention' and that patents on human organisms commodify life. This is a substantive patentable-subject-matter exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro-entity fee status for institutions of higher education
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions of higher education qualify for 'micro-entity' status when paying fees (an inventor who works for or assigns to a university may qualify for lower fees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision reduces filing/maintenance fee burdens for academic inventors and assigned inventions, promoting university-based innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify patent term extension filing deadline (Hatch-Waxman technical fix)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify when the 60-day period for applying for extended patent protection (under Hatch-Waxman) begins — e.g., if FDA notifies after normal business hours, the filing period should start the next business day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a narrow, technical amendment intended to remove uncertainty that can cost developers significant patent term restoration; it is described as budget-neutral and not a substantive change to the law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent abusive false-marking lawsuits
rubrics_metrics.description: Reform false-marking law so that nuisance lawsuits are curtailed (addressing the problem that after patents expire, marking errors led to lucrative nuisance suits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bill includes a 'common sense solution' to stop frivolous false-marking claims so companies can avoid costly recalls and focus resources on innovation and job creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study on gene patents and access to second opinions for genetic testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct the USPTO to study ways to remove barriers for patient access to second opinions on genetic testing for patented genes; study is not intended to express any congressional view on gene patent validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study would examine effects of gene patents on patient outcomes and options for providing independent confirmatory tests. It aims to address access and patient-protection concerns without prejudging legal issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain appropriations committee oversight while eliminating incentive to divert fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Design funding mechanisms that 'ensure the Appropriations and Judiciary Committees will continue to have oversight over the PTO' while removing the appropriators' incentive to divert fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manager's amendment attempts a compromise preserving oversight but making excess fee collections available to the PTO so appropriators lack scoring incentives to divert funds; balancing oversight and operational autonomy is a legislative design criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid turning PTO fee authority into unintended budgetary effects (CutGo and scoring considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be mindful of budget enforcement rules (e.g., CutGo) and CBO scoring anomalies when converting fee-authority structures between discretionary and mandatory spending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative drafters should recognize that accounting changes (discretionary vs. mandatory) may produce paper savings or trigger procedural objections; some supporters argue the manager's amendment avoids deficit impact while complying with rules through waivers.
